issue_context.title: Double forward slash on requests
issue_context.body:
Just curious if anyone is experiencing routes being generate with a double forward slash on requests (ending up within incoming requests to the Meilisearch server like POST //indexes//documents?primaryKey=id (taken from the console), it's resulting in 404's not found with the server, when built with the binary.
I'm not really sure where to go from here. When I generate a HTTP request via a rest client it all works fine. Anyone else have any issues?

Can’t remember the version I’m running. Don’t have it at hand.

Sorry didn’t realize it was related to the core.
comments:
Hey @Cmarenburg,

What do you mean by "routes being generated with a double slash"? Which tool do you use and which produces theses routes?

If you want you can call the `/version` route on the server and give us the informations.

Thank you :)

Hi @Kerollmops,

Version I am running is `0.10.1` I should probably update the title I initially thought posted it about the PHP-SDK thinking it was an issue best resolved under [there.](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch-php/issues/28)

It seems like the internal server does not respond to URL's with a double forward slash. Resulting in routes with 404's on valid HTTP actions. 

 Example `GET /version` works however `GET //version` results in a 404 not found. The issue I reported seems to be that the PHP-SDK generates requests with an extra forward slash in route params.  Maybe this an issue that belongs under both the core

What I've understood of the issue:

```bash
$ curl -iH 'Content-type: application/json' 'http://localhost:7700/stats'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
access-control-allow-origin: *
transfer-encoding: chunked
date: Tue, 05 May 2020 21:51:56 GMT

{"databaseSize":45056,"lastUpdate":null,"indexes":{}}

$ curl -iH 'Content-type: application/json' 'http://localhost:7700//stats'
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
access-control-allow-origin: *
transfer-encoding: chunked
date: Tue, 05 May 2020 21:51:59 GMT

$ curl -iH 'Content-type: application/json' 'http://localhost:7700/stats/'
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
access-control-allow-origin: *
transfer-encoding: chunked
date: Tue, 05 May 2020 21:53:36 GMT
```

Hey @curquiza,

Could you confirm this issue is still present on master, please? As we switched to Actix it as probably been fixed. I think double slashes is invalid but I think the final slash shouldn’t return a 404 but better be stripped by the router.

~PS: I will try to move this issue to the PHP repository.~ Done

@Kerollmops this issue is still on `master` 😕
For the slash at this end and in the middle of the URL.
@Kerollmops for me it's not a PHP issue related since it does not work with `curl`
@Cmarenburg if it's an issue you got with the PHP SDK, could you please detail your steps and the code you tried to execute?

Yeah, malformed request urls doens't work with curl nether, I think there is three things here:
  1. This is a normal behavior to refuse urls with double slashes.
  2. It is invalid behavior to refuse urls ending with a slash.
  3. If this is the PHP client which generate those urls, we must fix it.

I invoque @qdequele for the second point 🐉

We have the solution here: https://docs.rs/actix-web/3.0.0-alpha.1/actix_web/middleware/struct.NormalizePath.html 😉
I will fix it.
Does it also remove the trailling slash?
No, I will make a PR on this structure. Actix seems to be very open to PR.
@Kerollmops can you move back this issue to MeiliSearch repo then? 🙂

> @Cmarenburg if it's an issue you got with the PHP SDK, could you please detail your steps and the code you tried to execute?

I found the issue on my requests, the primary issue was I had a trailing slash in the environment variable.  So from my point of view I think that was the root cause of my original issue and point 2 of @Kerollmops just happened to exist and be discovered accidentally :)
